newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Yen vols soar as spot yen is pushed lower.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Yen vols soar as spot yen is pushed lower.

text.p: Dollar/yen and mark/yen option volatilities were sharply higher in European trade today, in line with new lows being set in spot yen.
Options dealers said trade here was busy with investors and market makers scrambling for cover as both spot dollar and mark touched over three-and-a-half year highs against the yen.

"People have been asking for strikes as high as 79 in mark/yen and 120 in dollar/yen in around three-months," said a U.S. bank options broker. "The market is preparing for the dollar to push higher and still seems bullish even at these higher vol levels."
One-month dollar/yen volatility was trading at 8.0/8.5 percent by the European midsession from 7.0/7.3 percent seen late Friday in Europe.
Further out, one-year volatility was quoted at 9.9/10.4 percent from 8.9/9.4 percent on Friday.

The one-month risk-reversal, the difference in implied volatility between relative calls and puts, was trading around par with a slight bias to yen puts from Friday's skew to yen calls at 0.1/0.4 percent.
Spot dollar/yen was trading at 114.20/25 at 1125 GMT compared with 113.22/27 late Friday in Europe.
Dealers said low yields, technical factors, and an uncertain political backdrop in Japan were providing enough reasons for invstors to dump yen.
Spot mark/yen was trading just shy of 75 yen in busy trade today, pushing one-month volatility to 6.7/7.0 percent against 6.0/6.3 percent Friday.
The risk reversal favoured mark calls at 0.1/0.4 percent from 0.0/0.3 on Friday.
In contrast, dollar/mark volatilities were little moved from Friday levels with spot stuck in familiar ranges above 1.52 marks in midsession trade.
One-month dollar/mark vol stood at 6.8/7.3 percent versus Friday's 6.7/7.0. The risk reversal favoured mark calls at 0.1/0.4 percent, little changed from 0.2/0.5 on Friday.
Cable vols were higher as the pound continued its climb against the dollar, trading above $1.61 at midday Europe. One-month vol was trading at 5.7/6.2 percent from 5.35/5.65.

"This is surprising given that people tend to take profits fairly quickly in sterling," said the U.S. bank dealer. "But the vol curve is beginning to flatten as people get comfortable with the trend."
